rungs.title: Rational first Chern classes and Cartier divisor classes are Hodge classes; F¹ is the kernel of the projection to 𝒪
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-24. Ω⁰ ≅ 𝒪; the stupid truncation 0 → F¹Ω^• → Ω^• → 𝒪[0] → 0 is short exact, so F¹ H^n_dR is exactly the kernel of H^n_dR → ℍ^n(𝒪[0]) (both inclusions); conjugation fixes de Rham images of rational classes. Hence the rational image of an integral degree-two class is a Hodge class iff it vanishes in H²(𝒪); first Chern classes do (exponential sequence), and so do classes of divisors of Cartier data (divisor–Chern, sign +). This is the known half in codimension one for Cartier divisors.

rungs.title: Unique factorization descends along faithfully flat local homomorphisms from a Noetherian local domain to a local UFD

rungs.title: The ideal sheaf of a prime divisor is an invertible sheaf represented by Cartier data whose divisor is minus the prime divisor
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. On a smooth projective integral complex scheme, the vanishing ideal sheaf of every prime divisor D = closure {ξ} is invertible (Tau Ceti IsInvertible) and is represented by Cartier data with divisor −D. Route: the vanishing ideal sheaf as S.Modules (HodgeLadder.Divisor.IdealSheaf); near each closed point of D a local equation π (height-one prime of the UFD local ring, principal after inverting one element on an affine open: HeightOneGenerator, LocalGenerator), and 1 away from D; local generation gives generating sections (generates_of_dividesVanishingAt) and hence invertibility (Tau Ceti ofClosedPoints); ord π = 1 at ξ and 0 at other codimension-one points (Mathlib's Scheme.ord), so the Cartier data with local equations π⁻¹ have divisor −D. Sign: the ideal sheaf is 𝒪(−D), so the divisor is −D; −[D] Hodge gives [D] Hodge.

rungs.title: Every invertible sheaf has a unit extension E with L^an ≅ E.sectionSheafOfModules
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. For invertible L on a smooth projective integral complex scheme, L^an is invertible (coherent by Oka, stalks free of rank one, X(ℂ) T1 hence Jacobson; Tau Ceti's closed-point criterion), so it has holomorphic frames σᵢ with σᵢ = gᵢⱼ • σⱼ. The middle sheaf N has sections (n, v) with n locally constant and g(b·)ᵢ·^n · v holomorphic on each Uᵢ (a local predicate); 0 → 𝒪ˣ → N → ℤ → 0 is short exact, with ℤ identified with locally constant functions (constIsoLC). E's chosen lifts of 1 have degree one and transitionUnit y x = vʸ/vˣ; the frames wˣᵢ • σᵢ (wˣᵢ = g(b·)ᵢ · vˣ) on the cover Oₓ ⊓ Uᵢ have E's transitions, and Frames.isoOfSameTransitions gives L^an ≅ E.section. This route does not use the stack's AnalytificationGenerates. Convention: docs/conventions.md, row 'Unit extension of a line bundle'.

rungs.title: Assembly: every prime divisor class is a Hodge class (CycleClassesAreHodgeOne)

rungs.title: Pullback on H^*(X; ℚ) is functorial and ℚ-linear: pullbackCoh (g ≫ h) = pullbackCoh g ∘ pullbackCoh h, pullbackCoh (𝟙 X) = id, bundled as pullbackCohLinear

For g : X ⟶ Y and h : Y ⟶ Z over Spec ℂ, pullbackCoh (g ≫ h) n α = pullbackCoh g n (pullbackCoh h n α) and pullbackCoh (𝟙 X) n α = α, exact, no sign, no scalar; pullbackCohLinear g n : H^n(X; ℚ) →ₗ[ℚ] H^n(X'; ℚ) bundles pullbackCoh with upstream's ℚ-structure fieldCohomologyModule ℚ (rfl), with _comp and _id. Route: conjExt is invariant under a natural iso of exact functors and compatible with composition of functors (Mathlib Ext.comp_mapExactFunctor, Ext.mapExactFunctor_comp_mk₀_natTransApp); (f₁ ≫ f₂)⁻¹ ≅ f₂⁻¹ ⋙ f₁⁻¹ and (𝟙 X)⁻¹ ≅ 𝟭 by leftAdjointUniq, with pullbackQX_comp and pullbackQX_id from the abstract triangle lemmas. rungs.title: deRhamPullback g n : H_dR^n(Y) →ₗ[ℂ] H_dR^n(X), the ℂ-linear extension of pullbackCoh through deRhamBaseChangeEquiv, compatible with ι, deRhamCup, deRhamConj, composition and identity
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-28. For g : X ⟶ Y between smooth projective integral X, Y over Spec ℂ, deRhamPullback g n : H_dR^n(Y) →ₗ[ℂ] H_dR^n(X) is deRhamBaseChangeEquiv X n ∘ (pullbackCohLinear g n).baseChange ℂ ∘ (deRhamBaseChangeEquiv Y n)⁻¹, defined from rational classes, so it carries no information about forms (agreement with a pullback of forms is de-rham-hypercohomology-pullback; F^p is hodge-filtration-pullback). Laws, all exact with no sign and no scalar: deRhamPullback g n (ι α) = ι (pullbackCoh g n α); (g ≫ h)^* = g^* ∘ₗ h^*; (𝟙 X)^* = id; the cup law for a + b = n in ℕ, bundled as (deRhamCupBilinear Y a b n _).compr₂ g^* = (deRhamCupBilinear X a b n _).compl₁₂ g^* g^* and pointwise as g^* (deRhamCup x y n _) = deRhamCup (g^* x) (g^* y) n _ (degree proofs (a : ℤ) + b = n by lia); deRhamConj X n (g^* x) = g^* (deRhamConj Y n x). Route: the ι law from deRhamBaseChangeEquiv_tmul at 1 ⊗ α; the rest on ι-images (pullbackCoh_comp, pullbackCoh_id, Cup.pullbackCoh_cup with fieldToDeRhamCohomology_cup, deRhamConj_fieldToDeRhamCohomology) extended by span_range_fieldToDeRhamCohomology_rat and LinearMap.ext_on (semilinear for conjugation, via deRhamConjSemilinear). Uniqueness: deRhamPullback_unique, a ℂ-linear map sending ι α to ι (pullbackCoh g n α) is deRhamPullback g n (the step de-rham-hypercohomology-pullback closes through). Kernel cost: about 27 s for the definition, 37 s for the ι law, 14 s for uniqueness, 3 to 10 s for each other law; a consumer-side Module ℚ shortcut instance does not reduce it (docs/gaps.md, Known weaknesses). Red team docs/sketches/de-rham-pullback.redteam.md, pass with changes.

For M finite free over a commutative ring R ([Module.Free R M] [Module.Finite R M], no Nontrivial R), spinAction_bijective: the action of CliffordAlgebra (QuadraticForm.dualProd R M) on ExteriorAlgebra R M by contraction plus wedge is bijective, and spinEquiv : CliffordAlgebra (dualProd R M) ≃ₐ[R] Module.End R (ExteriorAlgebra R M) is AlgEquiv.ofBijective of it, with spinEquiv_ι_apply (contractLeft v.1 y + ι v.2 * y, the registered sign) and spinEquiv_symm_spinGen. This is [GolyshevLuntsOrlov2001] Prop. 3.2.1(e) (Chevalley1954 not opened), proved the GLO way with the rank replaced by a count. Spanning, for any quadratic form: span_sublists_prod_eq_top (the products of the sublists of a spanning list L span the Clifford algebra; 2 ^ L.length of them, List.length_sublists). Surjectivity: basis_exteriorAlgebra_eq_list_prod writes each exterior basis monomial as a list product; the dual-basis contractions in increasing order send e_I to 1 and kill lower degrees, so (e_S * ·) ∘ c ∘ (e_{I∖T} * ·) is a matrix unit up to a sign u : ℤˣ (existential, as GLO's ±), basis_end_mem_range. Injectivity: End(∧M) is free of rank 2^(2n), and OrzechProperty.bijective_of_surjective_of_finrank_le applied to R^(2^(2n)) → Cl → End(∧M) (injective_spinAction_comp_sublistProd). The same count gives GLO 3.2.1(a) at full strength: linearIndependent_sublistProd_dualProd and the basis cliffordDualProdBasis; finrank_cliffordAlgebra_dualProd (Free and rank 2 ^ (2 * finrank R M), needs Nontrivial R because finrank = 1 over the zero ring), finrank_cliffordAlgebra_dualProd_int (rank 4 for M = ℤ), a consequence of the route end to end. Hypothesis test: spinAction_int_zmod_two_not_surjective (for the finite non-free ℤ-module ZMod 2 the dual is 0, every element acts by left multiplication, dual_int_zmod_two_eq_zero, spinAction_int_zmod_two_apply, and the projection onto ⋀¹ is not in the range), so Module.Free cannot be dropped; Module.Finite cannot be dropped because elements of the Clifford algebra have bounded degree shift (hand argument, sketch). Finite projective M would also work (localize); not needed for H¹ of a torus over ℤ or ℚ (docs/gaps.md). It is the one-line specialization of spinAction_mem_evenOdd_iff_of_injective (hypothesis Function.Injective (spinAction R M) only), and injective_spinAction_iff shows the criterion for all i is equivalent to injectivity. Equality forms: map_evenOdd_dualProd_eq_parityShift ((evenOdd Q i).map spinAction = parityShift R M i, [GolyshevLuntsOrlov2001] 4.3.6 'sends Cl^+ onto H^ev') and evenOdd_dualProd_eq_comap_parityShift (the preimage form); parityShift R M i is the iInf over j of Submodule.compatibleMaps (exteriorParity j) (exteriorParity (j + i)). rungs.title: The tensor product of sheaves of ℚ-vector spaces on X(ℂ) is exact in each variable
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. No holomorphy is assumed; a submersion written in charts as a coordinate projection satisfies hn. Proof: the two normal projections agree as maps of pairs (pullbackPairMap_comp_chartNormalProjectionPair, from hn), and both coclasses pull back the same class u_c of (ℂ^c, ℂ^c ∖ 0) (relativeCohomologyMap_comp), so no sign can enter.
